element_notes: 'keywords' define the overall DFT setup (functional, job type, SCF/grid settings, and relativistic options). For Cu-centered ligand complexes, consider scalar-relativistic treatment (e.g., ZORA/DKH) for d-electrons and use a sufficiently dense integration grid to capture metal–ligand interactions reliably.

'basis' specifies the basis sets used in the calculation. It can be assigned per element/atom and must be consistent with the chosen relativistic and methodological setup. For Cu complexes, it is common to use a higher-quality basis (and, when needed, an appropriate ECP or relativistic basis) on Cu, with compatible basis choices for the ligand atoms (e.g., C, F).

'cosmo' refers to the legacy COSMO solvation keywords. In newer ORCA versions, the recommended solvation models are CPCM and/or SMD; set the dielectric constant (epsilon) and related solvent parameters accordingly.

'output' controls print level and selected output sections (e.g., geometry, basis/matrices, SCF diagnostics, MO/orbital energies, densities, and population analyses). Configure output to support analysis of orbital energies, occupations, and MO coefficients when needed for downstream inspection or verification.
'method' defines some special methods or theory or basis sets that are important to carry out the calculation that need special attention.

'geometry' defines the molecular structure (coordinates plus charge/multiplicity and optional geometry controls). Here, the structure should represent a Cu-centered ligand complex containing Cu, C, and F atoms. Make a guess for such structures
